inline.s: The term embryonic breathing is no doubt familiar to everyone; it is
the name given to

that state in which the practitioner, in deep meditative stillness, breathes so subtly that neither he himself nor anyone about him can detect any movement of breath through nose and mouth. One who reaches this condition has every illness dispelled, is brimming with vitality, and feels as though his very body and mind have been entirely transformed, a qualitative leap upon the path of cultivation and the very goal for which every practitioner yearns.
The Immortal Scripture of Master Yin, Orthodox Lineage of the Eastern Flower, Imperial Pole, Opening and Closing, on Attaining the Way, says:
"By intently and earnestly focusing the mind on the paired gate of the Jiaji region, one naturally opens the single aperture of the Heavenly Heart
(Author's note: Heavenly Heart here refers to the spot one cun and three fen within the navel, where prenatal primal qi and primal yang gather together.)

. There one connects with the primordial ancestral qi of prenatal Heaven, and as a lodestone draws iron, so kindred natures draw near; this is what the True Man Zhuangzi meant by 'the breath of the true person reaches to the heels.'

Practiced long enough, each inhalation and exhalation enters the qi cavity, a wonder that arises of itself. In time the embryonic breath settles, the yin'e takes form, and the road to long life lies open."

This passage plainly instructs that by merely focusing the mind on the Jiaji region one can draw the primordial mixed qi of Heaven and Earth into the dantian, and in time naturally accomplish embryonic breathing.

[Yin'e] The Zhouyi Cantong Qi says: 'Nourish the yin'e with mindful tending, gather the spirit to perfect the body.' Zhu Yuanyu of the Qing dynasty annotates: 'The yin'e is none other than the primal spirit.'

Yet most of those in the qigong world who practice embryonic breathing have misread the meaning of the ancients' line 'of old the holy teacher passed on his oral formula, only gather the spirit into the qi cavity.' They take the busy, calculating conscious mind and use it to concentrate directly on the lower dantian, and then add regulated breathing, counting the breath, and holding the breath, hoping thereby to succeed. Not only do they fail of their wish, but a host of ill effects arise, exactly as Mr. Nan Huaijin thrice sharply rebukes: 'Men readily suffer seminal emission, and women are prone to flooding and spotting.'
My teacher has said:
In regulating breath one must regulate the true breath; in refining spirit one must refine the unrefined spirit.

The true breath is embryonic breathing; the unrefined spirit is the primal spirit. Both gathering the spirit and regulating the breath have their oral formulas; without them one fears the thinking consciousness will wrongly couple with the breath and congeal a phantom elixir, which harms the practitioner instead.
gather the spirit into the qi cavity

means that one must await the manifestation of the primal spirit and then gather it, bringing it down into the dantian, before true embryonic breathing is accomplished. The student should first hold to the Jiaji region so as to condense the primal spirit; when the merit is fully matured, then carry the spirit condensed there into the dantian and keep it there, and he will of himself attain the wondrous state of embryonic breathing. This is the right path of cultivation."

blocks.text: Third: the marvelous function of opening the barriers and unfolding the apertures

inline.s: To open the Greater and Lesser Orbital Cycles is a very popular topic in the qigong world today and the goal that the vast majority of practitioners pursue. But the orbital cycle methods now in vogue are for the most part the mind-led cycle and the meridian cycle. The former guides the inner sensation of qi by mind along the Conception and Governing vessels or the twelve regular meridians; for moving the blood and qi and inducing stillness it certainly has its effects
yet in truth it is only a stream of consciousness

The latter is the true qi circulating of itself along the meridians, needing no guidance of the mind, and its effects are excellent; but the route it travels is confined to the space between muscle and sinew, lacking depth and breadth, and so it too is not the true orbital cycle.

The so-called orbital cycle means that the true qi circulates unimpeded through the four limbs and hundred bones, the five organs and six viscera, down even to the eighty-four thousand pores of the whole body, the vast vital breath overflowing the four members. My teacher says in the Secret Transmission of Heavenly Origin:

"The method of opening the barriers lies wondrously in keeping the spirit on the single aperture of the paired gate. This aperture can connect the twelve meridians, can thread the eighty-four thousand pores, and pierce through the hundred joints of the limbs and the five organs and six viscera. When the spirit is condensed here and one practices holding the breath, in time the essence fills and the qi transforms, and this transformation of itself bursts open the three barriers, flows through the hundred channels, spreads freely into the four limbs, and every aperture becomes radiant. The Book of Changes says,
the yellow center penetrates and orders all, and the proper position abides in the body

, which is precisely what this means. At this point one has the verification of holding the breath until qi issues from each of the eighty-four thousand pores; this is for those of superior faculties and keen capacity. As for those of middling or lower capacity, or those whose practice is slack and slow, the barriers and apertures are hard to open; one must wait until the fire blazes in the dantian and the two kidneys seethe as if boiled, then practice according to the method, and only then can they be opened."

blocks.text: Fourth: the marvelous effect of replenishing the essential qi and restoring the youthful body

inline.s: Because of marriage and child-rearing and the toil of worldly affairs, by middle age a person has consumed the greater part of his essential qi, and often shows such symptoms as yin deficiency with blazing fire, shortness of breath and weariness of spirit. If one wishes to bring his qigong practice to a higher plane soon, the urgent need is to replenish the essential qi and return to the vigorous, flourishing health of youth.

As for the methods of replenishing essential qi, there are the tonic of medicine, the tonic of food, and the tonic of qi, that is, the method of qigong cultivation. But the first two demand a high level of medical knowledge before one may use them; otherwise an indiscriminate tonic leads only to dire consequence. How often one sees people recklessly take hot tonics such as ginseng and deer antler, and gorge themselves on chicken, duck, fish, and meat, calling it the fine art of nourishment. Little do they know that misapplied heating medicines only inflame the heart-fire, so that yin and yang fall out of balance and one suffers bleeding from nose and mouth and an unbearable agitation; and that an excess of rich food thickens the blood and qi, so that one falls prey to wasting-thirst, that is diabetes, and such intractable complaints as blockage of the heart and cerebral vessels. These disorders have already become the common diseases of our day, which people call the illnesses of affluence, and this truly deserves attention.

The ancients said, 'The tonic of medicine is not equal to the tonic of food, and the tonic of food is not equal to the tonic of qi,' and so it truly is. When the student, in holding to the Jiaji region, has reached a certain stage of merit, with its attendant marks of verification, and then practices further with the 'method of adding oil to restore the life force' (in truth the 'method of filling the essence and replenishing the marrow'), within a hundred days he can replenish the essential qi consumed over half a lifetime, and so radiate youth and grow fair again. My teacher says in the Secret Transmission of Heavenly Origin:

"In the womb the infant's Jiaji region is naturally open. Later, when the term is complete and birth takes place, the seven apertures abruptly open, and the qi, the vessels, the spirit, and the light no longer rise and fall by this passage, so that the blood grows foul and, gathering by degrees, gradually stagnates and congeals. Who would know that this very spot is the old road by which I first came into the world? If this aperture can be opened, no illness remains. A scholar who dwells in the world for decades, wearied by fame and profit and busied with affairs, never sparing his toil, gathers many ailments. If he can but know the secret of producing fire and kindling yang here, then whether old or young, his kidney-yang turns from weak to strong as easily as turning over the hand."

Of the manifold great functions of the Jiaji pass in cultivation I have set out above four in brief. As for the others, such as moistening the five viscera, benefiting the qi and nourishing the yin, replenishing the blood and calming the spirit, the student can truly experience them in the course of actual practice, so I will not belabor them. I hope this essay may awaken wide recognition among practitioners of the importance of the Jiaji pass, and that they then earnestly begin from the foundation of strengthening body and mind; only when the pure qian body is restored should they pursue the higher powers. Otherwise, to speak of 'the five eyes and the six supernormal faculties' while wearing a sickly countenance is no different from a madman's empty talk of dreams. And even if one gains a little, it is most unstable, or is but the morbid reflection of an imbalance of yin and yang in the body.
Finally,
let us
draw the whole essay together with the poem of Langranzi recorded in the ancient elixir scriptures:
The paired gates at the spine pierce through the crown; / of every path of practice this one holds the renown.
Swallow ever the Flower Pool's water bright; / the Primal Lord of the Purple Court soars to the height.
Let qi ever fill and the joints be opened through; / then the essence is full and the Valley Spirit holds true.
When shall you learn the deathless road, and how? / Be grateful to the one who first taught you till now.
